svg.aria-label: The revision mode, simple view. Boxes: academic-paper 3.2.0: Peer reviewer: the comments as a roadmap (agent); Draft writer: a patch (agent); You decide (stop); Citation compliance (agent); Revised draft, the rest as limitations (agent) | paper: Intake agent: you confirm (stop); Peer reviewer: the instructions as items, or, with none, a review of the manuscript (agent); A research question the materials do not answer, when an item names a part (stop); You approve the items, with no instructions (stop); Literature strategist, for a new reference (agent, only when needed); The citation loop does not close: another 8 rounds, or go on with the works named (stop); Visualization, for a figure (agent, only when needed); Draft writer: a patch per item (agent); Citation compliance (agent); Citation compliance once more, when a check fails (agent, only when needed); A claim the run cannot support, or a reference that cannot be confirmed (stop); The citation style to confirm, when more than half the entries fail the same check (stop); Peer reviewer: reading (agent); Draft writer: one pass (agent); Citation compliance for each later patch with a cited sentence: those sentences only (agent, only when needed); Draft writer: reference fix (agent, only when needed); A reference that cannot be confirmed (stop); Draft writer: compile fix (agent, only when needed); /writing: 4 agents, unless you said no at intake (agent, only when needed); End: the final message, with the /writing report and your reply, optional (agent); Draft writer: applies what you pick (agent, only when needed); Citation compliance: the sentences of the findings pass (agent, only when needed); Peer reviewer: reads the findings pass (agent, only when needed); Draft writer: compile fix (agent, only when needed); Draft writer: the anonymous copy, for a double-blind venue (agent, only when needed).

svg.text: Scripts and the session's own steps are left out. Not drawn because it is the same in every mode of paper: at every patch, a structural patch, a patch that does not apply or a failed script stops the run (a ruling of plan 5).
